current_example.title: Example: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination with Row Exchanges

q-20505.name: Question 1
q-20505.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+2y+6z=5 \\  & y-10z=-11 \\  & 4x+8y+13z=9\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
q-20505.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 6 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10 & -11 \\ 4 & 8 & 13 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 6 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10 & -11 \\ 4 & 8 & 13 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 6 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10 & -11 \\ 0 & 0 & -11 & -11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{11}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 6 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10 & -11 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-10676.name: Question 2
q-10676.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 19 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 13 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 & 25\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
q-10676.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 19 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 13 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 & 25\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 19 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 13 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 19 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 13 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & -20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 19 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 13 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+2z=19 \\  & y+2z=13 \\  & z=5,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=5$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
y+2(5)=13\,⟹\,y=13-10=3.
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=3$ and $z=5$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(3)+2(5)=19\,⟹\,x=6.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=6,y=3$, and $z=5.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨6,3,5⟩.$

q-73593.name: Question 3
q-73593.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+6y-3z=-1 \\  & -2x-12y+8z=1 \\  & -x-5y+4z=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
q-73593.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ -2 & -12 & 8 & 1 \\ -1 & -5 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ -2 & -12 & 8 & 1 \\ -1 & -5 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & -5 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the $3$rd row by $\frac{1}{2}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-73587.name: Question 4
q-73587.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -6 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
q-73587.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -6 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-3y=1 \\ y-z=-4 \\ z=1,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=1$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(1)=-4\,⟹\,y=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3(-3)=1\,⟹\,x=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-8$, $y=-3$, and $z=1.$
